Many injuries could be considered catastrophic. Generally, a catastrophic injury is defined as an injury that: Results in a temporary functional disability, such as paralysis, vision loss, or the ability to speak Causes a serious impairment or permanent disability Results in a person’s death A catastrophic injury may require extensive medical treatment for a considerably long period of time. The injury may require extended hospital stays and time spent in a rehabilitation center. The person may require life-long nursing and/or personal care because of a catastrophic injury. The victim may never return to their normal activities, including being able to care for their personal needs. Examples of injuries that could be considered catastrophic injuries include, but are not limited to: Damage to internal organs Spinal cord injuries Loss of limbs and amputations Complex fractures and broken bones Traumatic brain injury Hearing loss Chest injuries Severe burns Vision loss Crushing injuries Our Metairie catastrophic injury lawyers at the Law Office of John W. Redmann, L.L.C. fight to obtain the maximum compensation for your claim to provide for your future medical care, loss of income, and personal care. Common incidents that result in catastrophic injuries include, but are not limited to: Motorcycle accidents Animal attacks and dog bites Truck accidents Assault and other violent acts Car accidents Defective products Nursing home abuse Construction accidents Slip and fall accidents Workplace accidents Pedestrian accidents Sports and recreational activities Bicycle accidents Premises liability accidents After an accident, seek immediate medical treatment. Documenting your injuries is essential for a personal injury claim. Our Metairie catastrophic injury lawyers can help you with any type of catastrophic injury claim. We also help families who have lost a loved one file wrongful death claims. Louisiana personal injury laws define the types of damages you can seek for a catastrophic injury claim. Compensatory damages are divided into two categories: Economic Damages Your economic damages reimburse you for monetary losses through the date of settlement. They also compensate you for future damages you will incur because of the catastrophic injury. Examples of economic damages include: The cost of medical treatment and rehabilitative therapies Loss of earnings, including lost wages, earning capacity, and benefits Out-of-pocket expenses, including personal care and household services Nursing or skilled care, including long-term care facilities The value of your economic damages for a catastrophic injury can be difficult to calculate because of the ongoing care. Financial and medical experts provide estimates based on the severity of your impairments and other factors. Non-Economic Damages Catastrophic injuries cause extensive pain and suffering. Non-economic damages compensate you for your suffering. Examples of damages include: Emotional distress Physical pain Scarring and disfigurement Mental anguish Diminished quality of life Impairment and disability Loss of enjoyment of life Putting a value on pain and suffering is difficult because everyone experiences catastrophic injuries differently. The type and severity of your injury directly impact your level of suffering. Our Metairie catastrophic injury lawyers understand the complex nature of non-economic damages and how to use the evidence in your case to develop a compelling argument for maximum compensation. Does Comparative Fault Apply in Catastrophic Injury Cases in Louisiana? Louisiana has a pure comparative negligence law. You are not barred from receiving compensation if you are partially to blame for causing your injury. However, the damages you receive are based on your level of fault for causing the accident. For example, the jurors in your case determine you are 25% to blame for causing the accident that resulted in your catastrophic injury. Instead of receiving the total amount of the damages award, the judge reduces the damages by 25%. Every dollar in your damages award is crucial in a catastrophic injury claim. You need maximum compensation to provide for your needs. Therefore, you do not want to say anything that could be misinterpreted as fault. Talking with an insurance representative without legal counsel is not recommended. Many factors impact the value of your catastrophic injury case. Factors that could affect the value of your damages include: The type of injury you sustain The severity of the impairment caused by the catastrophic injury The duration of your recovery period Your ability to perform activities of daily living (i.e., bathing, dressing, grooming, etc.) Whether you can perform any work to earn an income The level of scarring and disfigurement The parties involved in your case The availability of insurance coverage and the policy limits Your liability for causing your injuries Our Metairie catastrophic injury attorneys analyze all factors in your case. We work to minimize the impact of factors that could lower the value of your claim while using the positive factors to maximize your settlement. Most personal injury lawyers in Metairie accept cases for a contingency fee. A contingency fee is based on the amount the attorney recovers for the claim. Instead of charging an upfront fee, they receive a percentage of the settlement or jury verdict. If they do not win the case, the client does not owe any attorney’s fees. If you have questions about a contingency fee or catastrophic injury claim, schedule a free consultation to discuss your case with an attorney. What is the Deadline for Filing a Catastrophic Injury Claim in Louisiana? The statute of limitations in Louisiana is two years for most personal injury cases. Missing the filing deadline for a personal injury lawsuit can result in losing your legal right to pursue a court claim. The judge can dismiss lawsuits filed after the deadline without considering the merits of the case. Catastrophic injury claims are extremely complicated. Contacting a Metairie personal injury attorney as soon as possible after the accident gives your lawyer time to investigate the case and prepare a lawsuit before the deadline approaches.
